examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Magnitude of a Vector-Valued Function
examples.problem: Find $\left|\mathbf r\left(4\right)\right|$ given that $\mathbf r(t)  = \left\langle 2-t, 2\sqrt{t}, \, t-1\right\rangle,$
examples.worked_solution:
Evaluating the function at $t=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(4) & =⟨2-4,\,2\sqrt{4},\,4-1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,4,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(4)| & =\sqrt{{(-2)}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{29}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: What is the value of $f(t)=⟨\sqrt{t+1},\,{t}^{2}-3,\,1-t⟩$ at $t=1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t=1$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =⟨\sqrt{1+1},{1}^{2}-3,1-1⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2},1-3,1-1⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2},-2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the value of $f(t)$ at $t=1$ is the vector $⟨\sqrt{2},-2,0⟩.$
